summary: Sixty Quid Bloke Listen, I have no new opinions about the football. I do, however, have thoughts about the media, and reporting, and what constitutes an emergency. People, podcasters, often joke about the ol’ emergency podcast. My kind of emergency podcast is one that fills the gap between, usually, Friday – when I run out of things to listen to – and after midnight on Monday, when a lot of my subscriptions drop an episode. (So a shoutout to Eggpod Express, which is dropping on Sunday mornings—perfect, super.) Where was I? Oh yes. Nothing to listen to. Eggpod Express was consumed before I got out of bed, and showering in silence is not something I can do, so I went to BBC Sounds (and, yeah, I’ve more or less listened to everything on there) and put on some live radio. First time in a long, long while. Radio 4 is best avoided on Sunday morning, so it was Five Live*, and inevitably, they were talking about the football. Now, if you’d asked me, I’d have said a few things about this World Cup. Number one being, boo USA, boycott 💨💨. Number two being boo FIFA, boycott that corrupt arsehole, and boo ticket prices, airfares, all that stuff. Also, pick a cooler country, you arseholes, and stopit with the creeping advert breaks. One cannot help but notice that the “drinks interval” has turned the game into one of four quarters, which is what America has wanted all along. I don’t know how ITV have managed to resist the temptation to drop in a few extra ads. But back up a bit. Boo ticket prices. I saw BBC reporting just the other day that was talking about tickets costing $1000 and more, and that the fans, as always, were being rinsed. (I get out my tiny violin for this, because football fans are always complaining about being rinsed and there is one simple trick they could use – yep, the boycott – but they never do.) But then I was listening to the radio this morning and they were interviewing a Scotland fan who was cock-a-hoop, and he revealed that he’d paid £60 for his ticket, and that if you bought home-and-away on a kind of World Cup loyalty scheme, you could follow your team all the way to the final for £60 a pop. Which – listen, I’m still my Dad saying, how much? – but sixty quid is not a thousand dollars. And if you’re the kind of fan who can afford all the air fares and the hotels, sure, you’re going to pay £60 for a match ticket in a heartbeat. That’s a trivial extra expense. But not only was this the first I’d heard of it, but the Five Live interviewer also seemed not to know about it. Which is basically his job. Anyway, I’m glad it’s all on in the middle of the night. *I don’t know if it’s even still called that. #football #media #reporting #WorldCup

summary: Sixty Quid Bloke Listen, I have no new opinions about the football. I do, however, have thoughts about the media, and reporting, and what constitutes an emergency. People, podcasters, often joke about the ol’ emergency podcast. My kind of emergency podcast is one that fills the gap between, usually, Friday – when I run out of things to listen to – and after midnight on Monday, when a lot of my subscriptions drop an episode. (So a shoutout to Eggpod Express, which is dropping on Sunday mornings—perfect, super.) Where was I? Oh yes. Nothing to listen to. Eggpod Express was consumed before I got out of bed, and showering in silence is not something I can do, so I went to BBC Sounds (and, yeah, I’ve more or less listened to everything on there) and put on some live radio. First time in a long, long while. Radio 4 is best avoided on Sunday morning, so it was Five Live*, and inevitably, they were talking about the football. Now, if you’d asked me, I’d have said a few things about this World Cup. Number one being, boo USA, boycott 💨💨. Number two being boo FIFA, boycott that corrupt arsehole, and boo ticket prices, airfares, all that stuff. Also, pick a cooler country, you arseholes, and stopit with the creeping advert breaks. One cannot help but notice that the “drinks interval” has turned the game into one of four quarters, which is what America has wanted all along. I don’t know how ITV have managed to resist the temptation to drop in a few extra ads. But back up a bit. Boo ticket prices. I saw BBC reporting just the other day that was talking about tickets costing $1000 and more, and that the fans, as always, were being rinsed. (I get out my tiny violin for this, because football fans are always complaining about being rinsed and there is one simple trick they could use – yep, the boycott – but they never do.) But then I was listening to the radio this morning and they were interviewing a Scotland fan who was cock-a-hoop, and he revealed that he’d paid £60 for his ticket, and that if you bought home-and-away on a kind of World Cup loyalty scheme, you could follow your team all the way to the final for £60 a pop. Which – listen, I’m still my Dad saying, how much? – but sixty quid is not a thousand dollars. And if you’re the kind of fan who can afford all the air fares and the hotels, sure, you’re going to pay £60 for a match ticket in a heartbeat. That’s a trivial extra expense. But not only was this the first I’d heard of it, but the Five Live interviewer also seemed not to know about it. Which is basically his job. Anyway, I’m glad it’s all on in the middle of the night. *I don’t know if it’s even still called that. #football #media #reporting #WorldCup
